title: The name lane
goal: Type a name capitalized with a `#` stroke and then the outline of its sounds: which outlines the dictionary holds for it, what the solver does when it holds none, and what to strike when a name has no pronunciation.

blocks.x: A name has two ways in. The ordinary one: the lowercase word, capitalized by [[KPA]] before it ([Punctuation](#/ref/punctuation)). The **name lane**: the stroke `#` alone, struck as a stroke of its own (it types nothing), then the name struck as the rules strike its lowercase word. `#` then `TKAPBL` types *Daniel*; `TKAPBL` alone is still *daniel*. Nothing in the lane is a new way of striking: it is the sounds you already know, behind one extra stroke.

items: **The lane stroke is `#` alone**, the number bar with nothing else down, struck as its own stroke. It is a built-in entry that **types nothing** (`{}`, in `01-lyk-commands.json`), so no `#` appears before the name, and a `#` with nothing after it types nothing at all. `#` held with other keys (`#KAT`) is not it: that is the number-key form, digits as ever.

**What follows it is a name, for every run the dictionaries do not list.** A name is read from the names alone (below), never from the ordinary words: `#` then `KOPL/+PU/+TER` is not *Computer* but the name that sounds likeliest. It lasts for the run right after the `#` only: the next word after the name is ordinary again. To type a literal `#`, give it a stroke of your own in your own dictionary (`#/#` is free) and strike that.

**The first stroke after `#` has no `+`**, as the first stroke of any word; every stroke after it carries `+`, as ever: `#`, then `AER/+O/+SPHEUT` is *Aerosmith*. A lone `+` locks, a `+*` stars the stroke before, and the endings of the [suffix table](#/ref/suffixes) go on: `AER/+O/+SPHEUT/+-S` after the `#` is *Aerosmiths*.

**Lowercase is leaving out the `#` stroke.** `HRO*ERD` lowercases the name just typed, as it does a capital from `KPA`. A name written other than with a capital first letter is written as the list has it (*McDonald*, *iPad*).
**The lane costs one stroke**, the `#`, which types nothing. A name that is also a word keeps its place in the one-stroke policy: its word is one stroke, the name is that stroke after a `#`.

blocks.x: The lane's list is Lapwing's proper nouns (`lapwing-prefixed-proper-nouns.json` and `lapwing-proper-nouns.json`) and every word Plover and Lapwing write only capitalized ([how names are counted](#/ref/how-stroke-setup)). A text is left out when it is a plain lowercase word (the file holds *college*) or an acronym (*NBC*, *HTML*: all capitals). A name's key is its lowercase letters; how common it is comes from the subtitle counts, as for words.
The dictionary: generated, never borrowed where the rules can strike the name

`build` writes `03-lyk-names.json`, numbered ahead of the solver (`05-`) so the dictionary answers where the solver would guess. Every entry is `#/` and an outline lyk's own rules give the lowercase name, from these sources, earlier first. An outline already held by an earlier source or a commoner name is not taken again.

head: Source
Entries for a name
rows: if lyk has the lowercase word: every outline of its words, short, alternates and extras entries (`#/` + [[daniel|TKAPBL]] is *Daniel*; nothing new to learn)
the plain outline and the spelling variant of every pronunciation the name has (a name said two ways gets both)
one syllable a stroke, for every pronunciation ([syllables](#/ref/syllables))
the cheapest 3 two-stroke, 2 three-stroke and 1 four-stroke ways to write its sounds, for every pronunciation

a name with **no pronunciation**: the cheapest ways to write its letters as joined strokes (4 of one stroke, 4 of two, 2 of three, 1 of four, as the spelled backups do), each vowel as the spelling gives it

blocks.x: Only a name none of these can strike (more than one word, a digit, a dot) is **borrowed**: Lapwing's outline after `#/`, in the separate file `03-lyk-names-borrowed.json` so it is never mistaken for lyk's, and never an outline a lyk entry holds. A name of more than one word is also two names: *Adam Neely* is the lane twice, `#/` *Adam* then `#/` *Neely*.

No entry in the lane can shadow a normal entry: every one starts with the stroke `#` alone, and no other file does. The lone `#` itself is the silent built-in; each `#/...` entry is a longer match and wins over it. `cargo test` asserts it against every generated entry and the reserved strokes.
When the dictionary has nothing: the name solver

A run struck right after a `#` that no file lists goes to the [solver](#/ref/fallback), which knows it follows a `#` (below) and reads it from **a second model that holds the names alone**, never the ordinary words or the morphemes: the same matching, costs, pieces, locks and late star as [the solver](#/ref/fallback), a name's rarity from its place among the names, and no word before it re-ranking the readings. Struck by its sounds, a name lands on its name:

blocks.x: Counts are from the current `build`: 10,622 names, 92,772 lyk entries, 2,685 borrowed entries. A letter-to-sound reading of a name with no pronunciation is not built: the spelling reading above is a deterministic stand-in that follows the spelled backups' chunks.

keymux keeps the strokes you struck before the one it is translating (its **stroke history**, cleared by a key press, typing by hand or a window change), and a plugin can read them. The solver reads the stroke just before the run it is asked about: if that stroke is `#` alone, the run is a name and is read from the names; any other stroke, or none, and it is an ordinary run. Nothing about `#` is known to keymux itself. A dictionary entry `#/...` is found first, as any entry ahead of the solver is, and the longest entry matches: a `#/` entry of your own dictionary still wins. A `#` entry of your own (`"#": "#"`) shadows the silent one: the `#` types, and the name lane still works, with a `#` in front of every name.

cargo run --release -- solve --name 'AER/+O/+SPHEUT'  # the name lane (the run after a lone #), every reading
cargo run --release -- solve --names 10             # strike every 10th name by sounds and by spelling
cargo run --release -- build                         # writes 03-lyk-names.json and 03-lyk-names-borrowed.json
